gloss: main argument; main discussion; the body (of a discourse)

definitions.gloss: main argument; main discussion; the body of a discourse
definitions.explanation: The central part of an argument, essay, or speech, as opposed to the introduction or digressions; also the main point one wishes to make. Common in academic and formal writing.

examples.english: to get to the main point.

examples.japanese: {前置|まえお}きはこのくらいにして、{本論|ほんろん}に{移|うつ}ろう。
examples.english: Enough preamble; let's move on to the main discussion.

examples.japanese: この{論文|ろんぶん}の{本論|ほんろん}では、{三|みっ}つの{原因|げんいん}について{詳|くわ}しく{述|の}べる。
examples.english: The body of this paper discusses three causes in detail.

notes:
Combines {本|ほん} (main, principal) + {論|ろん} (argument, discussion). The core part of a discussion or essay, distinct from the introduction or side topics; also the main point itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本論|ほんろん}に{入|はい}る: to get to the main subject
- {本論|ほんろん}に{移|うつ}る: to move on to the main discussion
- {本論|ほんろん}から{外|はず}れる: to stray from the main point

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {序論|じょろん}: introduction — the opening section that precedes the {本論|ほんろん}
- {結論|けつろん}: conclusion — the closing section that follows it
